ROBERT HOOKE AN THEODOR HAAK FÜR LEIBNIZ

[[801.1]] 227b. ROBERT HOOKE AN THEODOR HAAK FÜR LEIBNIZ

[[801.2]] [London, 22. Juli 1680.] [223a.228a.]

[[801.17]] S^#'r

[[801.18]] I am extreamly pleasd to finde by yo^#'r letter that D^#'r Leibniz (the acutnesse of whose

[[801.19]] invention and solidity of Judgment I very much admire and hono^#'r) has the same apprehensions

[[801.20]] w^#'t^#'h me concerning the usefullnesse of A philosophicall language and character. An attempt at

[[801.21]] w^#'c^#'h the late learned Bishop D^#'r Wilkins published in his book called the Reall Character etc. For

[[801.22]] though that excellent person has not carryed it soe farr and to the height it is possible to be

[[801.23]] improved for that end, yet what he did was not w^#'t^#'hout a prospect that way, and whilst he was

[[801.24]] composing of it we had many discourses to that purpose (for I had the happynesse to be w^#'t^#'h him

[[801.25]] a great part of the time that he was compiling it and have had many debates w^#'t^#'h him of that

[[801.26]] particular) though I never before I saw your letter heard in the least that it was the opinion of D^#'r

[[801.27]] Leibnitz. And though I could not Prevaile w^#'t^#'h that Person to modell it according to some Ideas

[[801.28]] of it which I then conceived yet since his Death I have spent some thoughts upon it and have

[[801.29]] formed an Idea of it which will shorten it at least half in half, and make it applicable and usefull

[[801.30]] not only for common Discourse and keeping Correspondence but for the strict and philosophicall

[[801.31]] way of Reasoning and Inquiry. Nor am I ignorant that the same method of Ratiocination

[[802.1]] and Demonstration which is made use of in Geometry and for finding out the affections and

[[802.2]] proprietys of quantity may also be applyed to the search after the proprietys affections and

[[802.3]] causes of any other subject where we can arrive to a certain knowledge of the principles of it,

[[802.4]] And even in the inquisition and manifestation of those principles the same method and art will

[[802.5]] assist us noe lesse then Algebra does Geometry or Arithmetick nor doe I doubt but that in

[[802.6]] naturall philosophy (for instance) the true proprietys of bodys the power of causes or motions,

[[802.7]] the effects resulting from conjunctions and the conjunctions and causes from the results may as

[[802.8]] certainly and demonstrably be evidenced from either of them Given as if both were seen

[[802.9]] together, and all the Intermediate time of operating. For the art of Reasoning both according to

[[802.10]] the Analytick and Synthetick method is not to be confined to the speculation of quantity,

[[802.11]] though that indeed be very extensive and comprise a very great part of man's Speculation, but

[[802.12]] is as boundlesse as the mind and Soule of man. Nor has this been unseen by severall Authours

[[802.13]] some whereof have made some essays towards it though very short of what may yet be done, by

[[802.14]] some that shall more thoroughly consider and examine it. Our learned Lord Bacon may be

[[802.15]] reconned among one of the best of that kind, And though he had the Infelicity to have some

[[802.16]] prejudice for mathematicall learning, yet the Extraordinary strength of his naturall and acquired

[[802.17]] parts carried him on Almost to a miracle in all the efforts of his undertakings. Severall excellent

[[802.18]] hints to this purpose may be found scatterd here and there in his Novum Organum and some

[[802.19]] other peices of his writings, But they are but Hints and doe yet need very much of thought and

[[802.20]] Invention to Produce them into a compleat Art and method. I question not but D^#'r Leibnitz has

[[802.21]] had very excellent thoughts to this Purpose. And I should be very glad to understand how farr

[[802.22]] he hath carryed it toward perfection. [ ... ]
